IBM.rationale: IBM's fundamental trajectory has deteriorated sharply. Q2 2026 revenue grew just 1.1% YoY to $17.16B, missing consensus of $17.86B, with Software growth collapsing to 5.1% from the 10%+ trajectory previously guided. Transaction Processing revenue declined 9% and Infrastructure revenue fell 7.4%. The Q2 miss triggered a 25% single-day crash — the worst in IBM's 115-year history — erasing ~$68B in market cap. Management admitted 'numerous large deals failed to close' due to enterprise budget shifts toward AI hardware infrastructure, a structural headwind not merely a timing issue. Guidance was cut to 4-5% revenue growth from 5%+. Multiple securities investigations are underway questioning management's prior assurances. While the stock has de-rated to 18.4x PE (floor of 365-day range), this reflects a legitimate re-pricing of a damaged growth thesis, not a buying opportunity. The margin step-change to 15.5% net margin has only ~3 months of data support and coincides with the period that produced the earnings miss — durability is unproven. Balance sheet leverage remains elevated (debt/equity 3.4x, current ratio 0.79-0.93, total debt ~$65-70B). Earnings yield of 5.4% sits below Baa corporate bond yields of 6.29%, offering no equity risk premium. The structural risk that enterprise AI infrastructure buildout cannibalizes IBM's software and mainframe spending — exemplified by Starbucks replacing IBM software with proprietary AI — represents a secular headwind to the core franchise. Near-term catalysts are negative: securities investigations, guidance credibility damage, and the need for multiple quarters of execution to restore confidence. The stock is making new relative lows ($206.65, just 3.8% above 365-day low of $199.19) with no fundamental floor visible.

IBM shares plummeted as much as 25% after the company issued a warning about Q2 earnings, citing lower-than-expected revenue due to clients shifting spending away from IBM products toward storage and memory infrastructure ahead of anticipated price increases. The stock drop represents the worst single day in IBM's 115-year history

On July 14, 2026, the company announced that, in contrast to assurances of '5-plus' Q2 2026 revenue growth, total revenue was up a paltry 1% and Infrastructure revenue declined 7%... CEO Krishna said 'numerous large deals failed to close'
Starbucks is developing proprietary AI systems to replace legacy software from Microsoft and IBM, targeting $400 million in annual software spending

IBM's competitive moat rests on three pillars: (1) deep enterprise trust built over 115 years, particularly in regulated industries with strict data sovereignty and compliance requirements; (2) the hybrid cloud platform stack assembled through Red Hat, HashiCorp, and IBM Cloud Paks, creating high switching costs once deployed; and (3) watsonx AI, which differentiates on governance, auditability, and on-premises deployment
